newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast spot prods mostly flat, buyers scarce - May 15.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast spot prods mostly flat, buyers scarce - May 15.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot refined product prices were mostly flat Thursday, with refiners avoiding the market until energy futures markets bottomed out, traders said.
On the NYMEX, June crude oil shed nine cents a barrel to $21.30 a barrel, while unleaded gasoline eased 0.34 cents a gallon to 64.04 cents a gallon.

NYMEX prices fell on news that Tosco Corp restarted its Trainer, Penn., refinery following a year-long upgrade which will the enable the facility to add 100,000 barrels a day of gasoline to East Coast gasoline markets.
Regional supplies weakened prices, with trade group American Petroleum Institute (API) reporting late Tuesday that West Coast gasoline stocks rose a 1.8 million barrels last week to 30.4 million.
++ GASOLINE: Traders pegged offers for May CARB gasoline at 63.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, flat from Wednesday.
Conventional grade unleaded also remained unchanged at 60/61 cents.
++ DISTILLATES: May CARB diesel fuel rose 0.50 cents to 60.50/61.50 cents amid talk "rack" prices in San Diego, Calif., rose two cents on supply disruptions at Tosco's Los Angeles refinery.
Rack prices indicate the cost of products at distribution terminals downstream of refineries.
Tosco officials declined comment, but traders said minor problems at one of the facility's diesel-making units tightened up supply, prompting higher rack prices.
